content: This medication is indicated for the treatment of chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC). The recommended dosage is 20 grams taken orally once daily. If persistent loose stools occur, the dosage should be reduced to 10 grams taken orally once daily. The safety and efficacy of this medication have not been fully established. The most common adverse reactions reported include upper respiratory tract infections (9%), flatulence (8%), urinary tract infections (5%), diarrhea (4%), increased blood creatinine phosphokinase levels (4%), abdominal distension (3%), abdominal pain (3%), and increased blood pressure (3%). Severe diarrhea and elevated creatinine kinase levels have been reported in 1% of cases. Post-marketing reports have also noted hypersensitivity reactions, such as rash and pruritus. This medication is contraindicated in individuals with known or suspected mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction or galactosemia. It is unknown whether maternal use of this drug results in fetal exposure. There is insufficient data from case reports on its use in pregnant women to evaluate the risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. Additionally, there is no available data on the presence of lactitol in human or animal milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production. It is also unclear whether the minimal systemic absorption of lactitol in adults results in clinically relevant exposure to breastfed infants. When prescribing this medication to breastfeeding mothers, healthcare providers should consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding, the mother’s clinical need for lactitol, and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant from lactitol or the underlying maternal condition. Lactitol is minimally absorbed in the small intestine. Any unabsorbed lactitol is expected to be degraded into organic acids in the colon and is minimally excreted in the feces. It is recommended to take this medication with meals. Oral medications should be administered at least two hours before or after taking lactitol to avoid potential interactions. The medication should be stored at a temperature of 20–25°C (68–77°F), with permissible excursions to 15–30°C (59–86°F). The above information is provided for general informational and educational purposes only. Individual treatment plans may vary, and formulary information is subject to change. For the most current information, contact the applicable plan provider.
